posts.title: Why Fitness Matters For a Muslim
posts.excerpt: Strength is not vanity. It supports worship, consistency, service, and emotional resilience.
paragraphs: Caring for your body is part of amanah. Better energy improves salah focus, learning, family responsibility, and community service.
The Prophet (peace be upon him) encouraged strength and beneficial living. Physical health supports disciplined worship and protects from burnout.
Fitness also builds sabr: turning up consistently, controlling desires, and doing hard things with sincerity. That mindset carries directly into deen and character.
Start simple: a realistic weekly routine, clean sleep, better hydration, and regular movement. Small habits done regularly are better than intense plans that collapse.
checklist: Set 3 realistic training days each week.
Keep one walk daily after prayer or meals.

posts.title: Easy Home Calisthenics Plan
posts.excerpt: No gym needed. Use this beginner-friendly structure to build strength at home in 20-30 minutes.
paragraphs: Warm-up first: 3 minutes brisk marching, arm circles, and bodyweight squats. Keep movements controlled and pain-free.
Run this circuit for 3 rounds with 60-90 seconds rest between rounds. Stop one or two reps before failure to keep form clean.
Progress slowly each week by adding 1-2 reps, or one extra round only when your recovery is good.
Pair this with a 20-minute walk on non-training days and consistent sleep for better results.
